title: I haven't seen a good French film since Blue Is the Warmest Colour (2013)

commenti.body: [removed]

Have you heard of Anatomy of a Fall? It’s a very French film that’s been getting a lot of praise for months now. It already had its limited theatrical release in America. And is winning critics awards this week.

There's a lot of great French cinema happening at the moment. Some I've watched recently:

* The Five Devils (2022)
* Portrait Of A Lady On Fire (2019)
* RAW (2017)
* Climax (2018)
* Anatomy Of A Fall (2023)
* Elle (2016)
* Saloum (2023)
* Passages (2023)
[removed]

And if *RAW* is your kind of movie, make sure to watch *Titane* be the same director, Julia Ducourneau. It's nothing short of a marvel in my humble opinion.

I’ve seen nearby a 100 French movies this year, many from the last decade. I’ll try to go back and rustle up a little list for ya. 

Just this week I saw 3 thrillers by one Dominik Moll, whom I’ve never heard about before. His ‘Only the animals’ is probably the best suspense story I’ve seen in months. Don’t read anything about it before watching it though. You’ll thank me later.
I didn't love Titans as much as Raw but I think I need to give it another go. That said "didn't love it" isn't exactly a criticism, it was really good.

I'm French and it's funny seeing the same films being recommended by foreigners all the time, but that's normal obviously most French films aren't released abroad. So off the top of my head I'd recommend Au Revoir Là-Haut(2017), Jusqu'à la Garde (2018), Le Chant du Loup (2019), Adieu les Cons(2020), Onoda: 10000 nuits dans la jungle(2021), Revoir Paris(2022), Yannick(2023).

Thanks!

Here we go with the anti-French cinema sentiment yet again. This idea that if you actually do some research you would understand that there are plenty of brilliant French films released every year. People just don't bother to seek them out or expand their horizons beyond mainstream cinema. Is it really too much asked for you to use Google or follow some international film festivals?
[removed]
I can't wait to see what this woman does next. She's bonkers.

Athena (2022) and Divines (2016) are excellent. Like La Haine, both are absolutely brutal, unflinching portrayals of marginalised communities in modern day France. The ending of Divines in particular is just unbelievably bleak and sad. If you've ever wanted to experience or understand life in an HLM (Habitation à Loyer Modéré - French housing projects), this is about as grim and harrowing as it gets.
I think of *Saloum* (2021) as Senegalese, but you’re right, it’s a coproduction.
The Beasts really an amazingly relevant, terrifyingly convincing story. Would highly recommended to anyone who loves a brooding suspenseful thriller.

Titane was the most memorable cinema experience I‘ve ever had watching a film without knowing what it’s about. I just went because I loved RAW and boy was that worth it.

Well, tastes are different after all and I can totally see and understand why people prefer RAW.

But I‘m also completely biased because ‚Titane is one of the best movies ever made.‘ is a hill I chose to die on.

One I haven't seen anyone else mention yet is Les Miserables (2019). 

It isn't the Victor Hugo story, and uses the name since it's the same neighborhood as Hugo's novel takes place and discusses class issues. It's kinda like a French version of Training Day with a new cop who has to deal with the corrupt group he's in, but that's a simplification and doesn't do the movie credit (not to say Training Day is bad, they're just different).
